Police searched an apartment in the Schöneberg district of Berlin near the scene of the attack in the early hours of Sunday, but said they had found no one there.

Describing Ballout as “generous, emotional, loving”, he said his son had lived with his mother, from whom Tawfik is divorced, and two of his three sisters. Ballout attended school until 10th grade, then bounced from job to job, in security or as a driver.

Police said the vehicle had struck multiple ⁠people after being driven into the Tiergarten. Shortly before 10pm the driver of the white minivan swerved into the park, close to where the route of the Pride march had been earlier in the day, hitting people on a path and crashing into a tree.

Bild cited a witness as saying that a man had emerged from the vehicle and fled on foot. A hunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states was under way across the capital on Sunday.

Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered in Berlin in warm summer sunshine to celebrate the Pride parade. It is known in Germany as Christopher Street Day (CSD), named after the site of the Stonewall Inn in New York City where riots against police raids touched off the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement. CSD was first held in West Berlin in 1979.

Berlin’s mayor, Kai Wegner, called the deadly assault “an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society”.

The parade on Saturday ran under the motto “taking a stand is hot”, which organisers said was “in response to increasing hostility” to LGBTQ+ people in Germany.

More than 80 floats and 50 groups on foot joined the procession through the city centre past Potsdamer Platz and the Victory Column monument in the Tiergarten, culminating in a rally at the Brandenburg Gate.

Before last year’s parade, Berlin LGBTQ+ organisations sounded the alarm that attacks had become more frequent while hard-won rights were under threat. Campaigners said a rise in hostility had accompanied the surge in support for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), now the most popular party in national opinion polls, as well as an increase in Islamist-inspired attacks.

Far-right leaders were also quick to comment on the attacks. The co-leader of the AfD Tino Chrupalla wrote on X: “We declare the war against Islamists. We will not allow religious extremists to divide our country with violence and intolerance!”

The president of the French far-right National Rally, Jordan Bardella, wrote: “The Islamist threat remains a major issue in Europe and continues to target what they hate most about our civilisation – and what we cherish so much – freedom.”

📄 Alamut’s World Heritage inscription to open new chapter for tourism in northwest Iran

📌 Qazvin, IRNA – A senior local investment official in Qazvin Province has said the inscription of Iran’s Alamut Castle and related fortifications on the UNESCO World Heritage List marks a turning point for tourism in the region, paving the way for new investment and preservation efforts.

Ali Farrokhzad, the provincial investment and employment chief, told IRNA on Tuesday that the inscription of Alamut as a World Heritage site would strengthen tourism appeal in Qazvin Province.
​
He noted that linking historical and natural attractions, such as Ovan Lake, hiking routes, and rural landscapes, could form a unified tourism chain and encourage visitors to extend their stays.
​
The official stressed that, with coordinated planning and support for investors, Qazvin’s diverse tourism capacities — from Alamut and Ovan Lake to hot springs, historic districts, and ecotourism — could position the province as a future hub for tourism, health services, and investment.
​
Iran’s Alamut Castle and related fortifications were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as the country’s 30th tangible cultural heritage site, following a decision adopted at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, on Friday.

🖥 Kremlin says Iran capable of defending its rights after Ukrainian assault on vessel

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov says Iran has the necessary capabilities to defend its rights, commenting on Ukraine’s drone attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea.

Responding to reporters on Monday, Peskov said Iran is an independent country that firmly defends its rights and possesses the necessary capabilities to do so.
​
He described Ukraine’s actions as aggressive, saying the government in Kiev has targeted different countries.
​
“Ukraine is attacking various countries. Previously, Ukraine attacked Germany by blowing up a facility of critically important energy infrastructure. Now it has attacked Iran, striking an Iranian vessel,” he said.
​
The Kremlin spokesperson also referred to Ukrainian drone strikes on facilities and terminals of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, noting that Kazakhstan is a joint owner of the oil pipeline consortium.
​
In separate remarks later on Monday, Peskov warned that Ukraine’s attack on the Iranian vessel represented another round of escalation by Kiev and could signal an expansion of the geographical scope of the conflict.
​
An Iranian commercial vessel, owned by the private sector and carrying rolled steel sheet cargo, came under a Ukrainian drone attack in the Caspian Sea on Saturday.
​
Denouncing the attack, the Iranian Foreign Ministry said it reflected Ukraine’s continued “irrational and hostile approach” towards Iran.
